input: The recommendation is a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision. The plant engineer owns the trial. The food plant uses 1885 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, and the equipment vendor projects that the retrofit will save 13% of that use, a derived saving of 245 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $351k. At an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $27k and the derived simple payback is 13 years: the retrofit returns $27k per year against a capital cost of $351k. The saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the payback rests on a projected saving and on a load profile with the peak month missing. The trial replaces the projection with a measured saving on a single line, at the cost of the metering and the trial period rather than the cost of the retrofit. A measured saving either supports the vendor figure or shows the gap between the projection and this plant, and the capital decision is then taken on the measured result. The trial is metered, so the saving it reports is a measured saving on the line where the trial runs, set against the use of that line over the trial period. No capital is committed while the trial runs, and the plant is not asked to carry the retrofit on the strength of a projection in the meantime. The payback at the vendor figure is long, and a long payback is the case where the difference between a projected saving and a measured saving decides whether the capital should be committed at all.
